<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">13 Tammuz,</t>
    <t s="2">5742*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that while even one person studying Torah draws down Divine revelation, the drawing down through Torah study of many (ten) is a loftier revelation, analogous to communal prayer drawing down the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Ten who sit and engage in Torah, the Shechinah dwells among them... even five... even three... even two... even one"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the leader of the generation, the Baal HaGeulah, explains in his maamar beginning with the words "This was given" for the first celebration of Yud-Beis Tammuz</t>
    <t s="2">(the year 5688)2,</t>
    <t s="3">that although3</t>
    <t s="4">even one who sits and engages in Torah</t>
    <t s="5">(and certainly two, three, and five)</t>
    <t s="6">draws down a revelation of G-dliness</t>
    <t s="7">("the Shechinah dwells"4),</t>
    <t s="8">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="9">the drawing down through Torah study of many</t>
    <t s="10">(ten5)</t>
    <t s="11">is a loftier drawing down6.</t>
    <t s="12">For just as regarding prayer, our sages, of blessed memory, said7</t>
    <t s="13">"The prayer of the many is not rejected," as it is stated8</t>
    <t s="14">"Behold, G-d is mighty and does not despise,"</t>
    <t s="15">for the many, in their prayer, draw down the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy9,</t>
    <t s="16">so too is it regarding Torah,</t>
    <t s="17">that through Torah study of many, a revelation of a higher light is drawn down.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the term "many" (rabbim) refers specifically to ten Jews, because ten Jews represent and include all ten types of Israel, constituting the greatest possible multitude.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the explanation of the expression of our sages, of blessed memory, "the prayer of the many"</t>
    <t s="1">[and in the maamar he uses the term "many" also regarding Torah],</t>
    <t s="2">even though it speaks regarding ten</t>
    <t s="3">[and the term "many" also applies to less than ten,</t>
    <t s="4">and on the other hand,</t>
    <t s="5">even ten is not the completeness of "many,"</t>
    <t s="6">for there is a greater multitude10],</t>
    <t s="7">is to be understood,</t>
    <t s="8">with an introduction:</t>
    <t s="9">that the reason that a matter done in the presence of ten Jews is the greatest public display</t>
    <t s="10">(and we do not find a distinction regarding public display between ten and more than ten)</t>
    <t s="11">is,</t>
    <t s="12">because ten Jews are11</t>
    <t s="13">analogous to and include the ten types of Israel</t>
    <t s="14">("your heads, your tribes... until the hewer of your wood and the drawer of your water"12),</t>
    <t s="15">and public display before ten Jews is like public display before all of Israel.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is that ten Jews are called by the name "many"</t>
    <t s="17">(simply),</t>
    <t s="18">the greatest multitude, than which there is no greater multitude.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
